'''Yury Kronn''' (April 22, 1935 – April 9, 2021), was a Soviet-born American radio-physicist and academic.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-03-14 |title=Dr. Yury Kronn - Faculty Member |url=https://quantumuniversity.com/faculty/dr-yury-kronn/ |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=Quantum University |language=en-US}}</ref> He is known for developing a theory of resonant [[non-linear]] interaction of light with matter, which was the basis for a physics text book, ''Resonant Nonlinear Interactions of Light with Matter''.<ref name="resonant_nonlinear_springer" />

In 1982, Kronn and ten other Russian dissidents organized a movement to foster trust and promote peace between the Soviet Union and the West.<ref name=nahaylo_group>{{cite news |title=Soviet peace group survives despite all the odds |first=Bohdan |last=Nahaylo |newspaper=The Spectator |date=December 20, 1983}}</ref>  Kronn chaired the Disarmament Section of the first Moscow International Symposium for Humanitarian Problems in 1987.<ref name=remnick_university>{{cite news |title=New 'University' Debuts in Moscow |first=David |last=Remnick |newspaper=Washington Post Foreign Service |date=April 2, 1988}}</ref>

In 2013, Kronn was appointed a faculty member of Quantum University in Honolulu, Hawaii,<ref>{{cite web|title=Teachers to inspire a new generation of health care practitioners|url=http://iquim.org/blog/teachers-to-inspire-a-new-generation-of-health-care-practitioners/|publisher=Quantum University|access-date=26 August 2013}}</ref> a school that is not [[educational accreditation|accredited]] in the United States.<ref>[http://files.hawaii.gov/auditor/Reports/2014/14-03.pdf Unaccredited institutions], Hawaii.gov</ref> Kronn died on April 9, 2021, at the age of 85.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Team |first=E. T. I. |title=Yury Kronn, (1935 - 2021) - ForeverMissed.com Online Memorials |url=https://www.forevermissed.com/yury-kronn/about |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=www.forevermissed.com |language=en}}</ref> Later in 2022 after his death a book titled the Science of Subtle Energy was published writtten by Kronn.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yury Kronn |url=https://www.simonandschuster.com/authors/Yury-Kronn/189178332 |access-date=2026-11-01 |website=Simon & Schuster |language=en}}</ref>

== Soviet dissident activities ==
In June 1982, with ten other dissidents, Kronn helped organize the Group to Establish Trust Between the U.S. and the USSR, a non-official movement for trust and peace between the Soviet Union and the West.<ref name=trust_group>{{cite web|title=Documents of the Soviet Groups to Establish Trust Between the U.S. and the U.S.S.R. |url=http://www.csce.gov/index.cfm?FuseAction=ContentRecords.ViewDetail&ContentRecord_id=409&ContentType=G&ContentRecordType=G&Region_id=101&Issue_id=0&CFId=70848716&CFToken=73023957 |date=May 22, 1984 |website=Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe |publisher=US Helsinki Commission |access-date=September 5, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201150837/http://www.csce.gov/index.cfm?FuseAction=ContentRecords.ViewDetail&ContentRecord_id=409&ContentType=G&ContentRecordType=G&Region_id=101&Issue_id=0&CFId=70848716&CFToken=73023957 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }}</ref>

The Trust Group avoided criticizing their own government's policies, both because they believed that criticism would generate opposition, and because it was illegal to do so.<ref name=ontario_visit>{{cite web |title= Members of Trust Group Visit Ontario |url= http://tpc.peacemagazine.org/241/members-of-trust-group-visit-ontario |last=Spencer  |first=Metta |date=June 1984 |website= Peace Magazine |publisher=Canadian Disarmament Information Service |access-date=July 3, 2013}}</ref> Instead, they suggested ways to improve relations between the superpowers based on the belief that improved trust could slow or stop the arms race. Their proposals included ideas for conversion of the military-industrial complexes on both sides by shifting to joint work on peaceful, humanitarian projects.<ref name=ontario_visit />

As a result of these and other actions, Soviet authorities applied pressure on Kronn.<ref name=satter_delirium >{{cite book | title= Age of Delirium, The Decline and Fall of the Soviet Union | last=Satter | first=David | year=1996 | publisher=Alfred A. Knopf| location=New York |pages=234–235, 240–245}}</ref> New York Times Moscow correspondent [[John F. Burns]] reported that Kronn, then known as Yury Khronopulo, had been warned at the institute where he was employed that he faced dismissal and possible prosecution for treason if his dissident activities continued.<ref name= burns_disarmament_group_harassed>{{cite news |title= An Independent Disarmament Group is Harassed in Moscow  |url= https://www.nytimes.com/1982/07/07/world/an-independent-disarmament-group-is-harassed-in-moscow.html |last=Burns  |first=John F. | date=July 7, 1982 |newspaper= New York Times |access-date=September 4, 2013}}</ref>

In the summer of 1982, while an international peace march was taking place in Moscow, assault charges were fabricated against Kronn and an associate, [[Yuri V. Medvedkov]].<ref name=trust_group/><ref name=satter_delirium /> The two were arrested on July 16 and held in prison by the Soviet security department, the [[KGB]], until July 31, 1982.<ref name=trust_group /><ref name=satter_delirium /> Despite attempts to silence him, Kronn persisted with his unsanctioned political activities. In 1987 he chaired the Disarmament Section of the first [[Moscow International Symposium for Humanitarian Problems]].<ref name=lee_limit_to_glasnost>{{cite news |title= Moscow Poll Finds Limit to 'Glasnost' - Soviets Say Kremlin Curbs Expression |last=Lee |first=Gary |date=December 21, 1987  |website= Washington Post Archives |publisher=Washington Post Foreign Service}}</ref>

== Patents ==
{{unreferenced section|date=November 2023}}
Five patents have been granted to Kronn; four in the Soviet Union and one in the US: 
* Method of Obtaining Holograms, USSR Patent No. 508142, (1975)
* Method of Transformation and Intensification of an Object's Image, USSR Patent No. 533254, (1976)
* A Method of Amplifying Superpower Laser Impulses, USSR Patent No. 2768756 (1979)
* A Method of Obtaining Light Impulses with a Steep Front, USSR Patent No.2876505 (1980)
* {{cite patent ||title=Antenna |country=US |number=4933679 |status=patent |invent1=Khronopulo, Yury |invent2=Gorbusky, Philip |gdate=12 June 1990}}
